questions.q: A data engineer runs PySpark code in a Fabric Notebook with no cluster configuration screen anywhere in the process. Why?
options: Fabric Notebooks attach to a Spark session backed by the workspace's capacity, abstracting cluster sizing behind the capacity/SKU system
Fabric Notebooks don't actually use Spark at all
Cluster configuration happens automatically outside of Fabric entirely, in a separate Azure resource
PySpark code cannot run in a Fabric Notebook without a cluster
questions.explain: Fabric Lesson 6/14: the compute is still Spark, but Fabric abstracts cluster management behind workspace capacity.

questions.q: A notebook's Delta table write fails partway through, after some files were already written. What is the table's queryable state afterward?
options: Unchanged — only fully committed transactions are ever visible, thanks to the Delta transaction log
Partially updated with the incomplete write visible to readers
Corrupted and unreadable until manually repaired
Automatically rolled back to a version from a week prior
questions.explain: Databricks Lesson 17's transaction log makes writes atomic — a failed write never becomes partially visible, in Fabric or Databricks.

questions.q: A team wants automated tests for their PySpark transformation logic before it runs in production. What approach applies, and does it differ between Fabric and Databricks?
options: Unit testing the transformation functions against small in-memory DataFrames — this works identically in either platform, since the transformation logic is portable Spark code
Testing is only possible in Databricks, never in Fabric
Testing requires a live production data load in both platforms
Fabric notebooks cannot be unit tested under any circumstances
questions.explain: Fabric Lesson 49's unit-testing approach applies the same way regardless of which platform's notebook runs the code.

questions.q: What determines the performance ceiling of Spark workloads running in a Fabric Notebook?
options: The Fabric capacity/SKU the workspace is assigned to
The notebook's file name
The number of Lakehouses in the tenant
The Power BI report layout
questions.explain: Capacity and SKU sizing (Fabric Lesson 14) governs the compute ceiling for Spark sessions backing Fabric Notebooks.

questions.q: Why does Delta Lake's ACID guarantee matter for a Fabric Notebook writing to a Lakehouse table, specifically?
options: It ensures concurrent or failed writes never leave readers seeing a half-written, inconsistent table
It has no practical effect inside Fabric, only inside Databricks
It only applies to Warehouse tables, not Lakehouse tables
It prevents any notebook from ever writing to a Delta table
questions.explain: Every Fabric Lakehouse table is a Delta table under OneLake, so Databricks Lesson 18's ACID guarantees apply directly.

questions.q: A scenario contrasts 'Fabric-specific abstraction' against 'general Spark/Delta concept that applies in Databricks too.' Which of these is the Fabric-specific piece?
options: The capacity-backed Spark session replacing manual cluster configuration
Delta Lake's transaction log making writes atomic
ACID guarantees on table writes
Portable PySpark transformation functions
questions.explain: The capacity/SKU-backed Spark session is Fabric's own abstraction; the Delta/Spark mechanics underneath are shared with Databricks.
